$comment: Cross-language conformance fixture for how a bound data row's cell is written into the field it lands in (issue #2639). Read by BOTH the engine gtest suite (engine/tests/scenario_data_test.cpp, via VAYU_ENGINE_SOURCE_DIR, through `bind_data_row` with row index 0) and the app's vitest suite (app/src/lib/variable-resolution.row.test.ts, through `previewRowBind`). Each case binds the row `{"v": cell}` into one field of the kind `fieldKind` names: `plain` a `text` body, `url` the request URL sent encoded, `header` the value of a header, `json` a `json` body, `xml` an `xml` body. `expected` is the field after the bind, byte for byte; a case with `refusal` instead is a row the bind refuses, and `refusal` is the engine's whole message. A token's encoding is decided by the literal text before it only: inside a JSON string the cell is escaped (quote, backslash, controls; non-ASCII and `/` as typed), outside one it is verbatim; in XML character data `&`, `<` and `>` are escaped, in an attribute the delimiter in force as well, inside CDATA only `]]>` is split, in a tag or attribute name nothing is, and in a comment or processing instruction the row is refused; in a header a CR or LF refuses the row; in a URL the cell is URL text encoded by Postman's set for the component it lands in.

cases.name: json: a quote inside a string is escaped (the issue's case)
json: a backslash inside a string is escaped
json: newline, tab and carriage return take their short escapes
json: other controls are \u00xx in lowercase hex, backspace and form feed short
json: non-ASCII, a slash and DEL pass as typed
json: outside a string the cell is written verbatim
json: an escaped quote in the template does not end the string
json: the escape flag does not carry across a token
json: a bare column binds by the same rule
xml: character data escapes &, < and >, not the apostrophe
xml: a double-quoted attribute escapes its own delimiter
xml: a single-quoted attribute escapes its own delimiter
xml: CDATA takes the cell byte for byte, splitting ]]>
xml: an attribute name is written verbatim
xml: a token straight after < is character data until the tag is read
xml: a declaration is stepped over
xml: after a CDATA section is character data again
xml: after a comment is character data again
xml: a delimiter half-read before a token completes after it
xml: a token in a comment is refused
cases.refusal: {{data.v}} sits inside an XML comment, where a bound value is not sent at all - and one carrying "-->" would end the comment and change the document instead, so the row is refused rather than bound somewhere it cannot be read

cases.name: xml: a token in a processing instruction is refused
cases.refusal: {{data.v}} sits inside an XML processing instruction, which is markup addressed to the parser rather than content - a bound value carrying "?>" would end it and change the document, so the row is refused rather than bound into markup

cases.name: header: a cell is written as it stands
header: CR LF in a cell is refused
cases.refusal: {{data.v}} is bound into a header, and data row 0 has a line break in that column - a CR or LF ends the header line rather than sitting in it, so the rest of the value would be read as headers of its own; the row is refused rather than sent forging a header

cases.name: header: a lone LF is refused too
cases.refusal: {{v}} is bound into a header, and data row 0 has a line break in that column - a CR or LF ends the header line rather than sitting in it, so the rest of the value would be read as headers of its own; the row is refused rather than sent forging a header

cases.name: plain: a text body takes the cell byte for byte
plain: a line break is ordinary content outside a header
url: a space in the path is %20
url: a quote in the path is encoded, not JSON-escaped
url: a cell's & and = split query pairs
url: a cell's ? in the path opens the query
url: non-ASCII in the query is UTF-8 percent-encoded
url: the fragment takes its own set
